key_insight: AgentOptics introduces an agentic AI that translates natural-language tasks into protocol-compliant actions across diverse optical hardware using a standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling high-fidelity autonomous control.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between language-driven intent and reliable device-level control in heterogeneous optical systems by providing a unified tool abstraction and benchmark to handle multi-step, role-aware coordination and reduce manual, error-prone intervention.
method: Define the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a structured interface for agents to issue, validate, and coordinate actions across instruments.
Implement 64 standardized MCP tools mapped to 8 representative optical devices via a tool abstraction layer for consistent command semantics and safety checks.
Construct a 410-task benchmark to evaluate natural-language understanding, role-aware responses, multi-step orchestration, and execution fidelity on real/representative hardware.
impact: Makes optical-lab automation accessible to AI practitioners by standardizing device interactions and providing a benchmark for training and evaluating agentic controllers, accelerating reproducible experiments and safe deployment of AI-driven hardware control.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram: Natural-language user → Agent → MCP tool layer → 8 optical devices (with feedback loops).

paper_title: Agentic AI for Scalable and Robust Optical Systems Control
paper_authors: Zehao Wang, Mingzhe Han, Wei Cheng, Yue-Kai Huang, Philip Ji
